The monsoon trough remains north and has left the Marianas in a dry
slot with only isolated showers and thunderstorms. The monsoon trough
may shift slowly closer but will likely remain offshore, so only an
increase to scattered showers looks possible Thursday night and maybe
Friday night. However, the monsoon trough is expected to slowly
weaken over the next few days as what remains of Invest 97W gets
sheared apart and the TUTT cell to the north weakens and shifts west.
Southwest winds will then drop off and allow for afternoon island 
effect showers and isolated thunderstorms as soon as Saturday 
afternoon, possibly lasting through the rest of the forecast period
if winds remain light. Outside of the island effect, shower coverage
is expected to stay isolated.

Marine/Surf...
For the coastal waters, showers may become scattered late tonight. 
Gentle to moderate southwest winds are expected for the next two 
nights with moderate to fresh winds Thursday. Winds look to start 
decreasing Friday and into the weekend. This may allow island effect 
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms to drift over the 
coastal waters northeast of the islands Saturday afternoon. Seas of 
around 6 feet tonight will remain steady before gradually decreasing 
sometime Friday or Friday night. Swells consist of mainly a monsoonal
southwest swell and a small east trade swell. Isolated thunderstorms
are expected through at least Saturday afternoon. 

Along the coastline, there will be a moderate risk of rip currents 
along south and west facing reefs of the Marianas. There will also be
a moderate risk of lightning through at least Saturday afternoon. 
Observational data showed shoulder to head high surf today on west 
facing reefs which should continue through tonight.

Tropical Systems...
A weak circulation looks to be in the early stages of LLCC
cyclogenesis west-southwest of Kosrae/southeast of Pohnpei near 4.6N
160.3E. This circulation has become a little "tighter" since this
morning, with a corresponding less broad cyclonic flow. Ensembles
suggest little to no development is expected with this system in the
short term. However, it may amplify the ongoing monsoon flow over
Palau and Yap towards the end of the forecast period. The key item 
to watch we think will be the cross equatorial flow, as JTWC (the 
Joint Typhoon Warning Center) noted. We agree with this assessment 
and will continue to monitor both of those items of interest. At the 
very least, it'll likely remain as a LPA (Low Pressure Area) and 
increase shower and thunderstorm potential at Kosrae and Pohnpei over
the next 48 hours or so.

Eastern Micronesia...
Pohnpei and Kosrae stand the best chance of seeing some rainfall the
next few days, with some thunderstorms mixed in from time to time as
well. This is due to a (slowly) developing area of low pressure 
west-southwest of Kosrae. The models lift this feature up over 
Pohnpei the next few days, ejecting it north-northwest after its 
passage. This rainfall potential will be aided by the cross- 
equatorial flow that developed. Here, sustained winds have been 
mostly in the 10 to 15 knot range, helping to advect a southeast to 
southwesterly swell into the region. However, the swell has been tame
enough to not pose any beach hazards. Overall, look for increasing 
rainfall potential with light to gentle winds gradually veering from 
southerly to a more westerly direction by the weekend. After the 
circulation departs the region, somewhat drier weather will return to
both Pohnpei and Kosrae. 

Majuro remains a little more tricky of a forecast as a nearby surface
trough has only modest convergence. Still, this convergence is
sufficient enough for low-end scattered shower development just to
the north and northeast. With this in mind, went with scattered 
showers (30 percent probabilities) for tonight, with shower coverage 
dropping back to isolated for tomorrow. The isolated shower coverage 
will persist through the weekend, with currently, no higher rainfall 
potential in sight. This lower rainfall potential, combined with 
light winds, will allow afternoon high temperatures to push 90 
degrees through the weekend, possibly longer.

Variable winds in the light to gentle range can be expected near the
circulation west-southwest of Kosrae the next few days, with light 
easterlies at Majuro. Seas will remain in the 4 to 6 foot range.

Western Micronesia...
A broad, west-to-east elongated circulation remains loosely centered
southeast of Pohnpei this afternoon. Converging north to 
northwesterly flow across much of Chuuk State is expected to produce 
numerous to widespread locally heavy showers and isolated 
thunderstorms across Weno tonight. There is some uncertainty on the
